title: incident-forensics-evidence-handoff-procedure-2026
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview
--------
This document defines the standard procedure for collecting, preserving, and handing off forensic evidence after a major service incident at Redwood Inference. It focuses on: SLO/error-budget impact artifacts, capacity and topology evidence, telemetry and trace capture, and chain-of-custody/audit steps so evidence is admissible for post-incident analysis, legal requests, and reliability initiatives. This is an operational runbook intended to be executed by SRE oncall and the incident commander.

Scope
-----
- Services covered: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache, request-proxy, batch-ingest
- Incident severity: Sev1 / Sev2 that triggers a full post-incident review (PIR) or legal/data requests
- Evidence types: logs, traces, metrics, profiling snapshots, model artifacts, autoscale events, cloud provider capacity events, routing and rollout state

Owner & Contacts
------------------
- Primary owner: SRE Incident Forensics Squad (contact on-call: #sre-oncall)
- Service owners: listed in service-catalog page (see related_pages below)
- Legal / Privacy escalation: security@redwood.com (required for any PII exposure)

Why this matters
------------------
- Ensures consistent SLO impact measurement for runbook improvements and error-budget accounting.
- Preserves evidence needed for capacity planning exercises and reliability initiatives.
- Provides auditable chain of custody for internal/external compliance reviews.

Pre-incident / Prerequisites
---------------------------
1) Ensure incident ID and canonical artifact bucket are created at incident start: INCIDENT_ID format rdx-YYYYMMDD-NNN (runbook automation does this).
2) Ensure oncall has access to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/ and temporary encryption key via KMS alias: alias/incident-enc.
3) Ensure automation token (read-only) for telemetry APIs is available in vault path secret/incidents/automation-token.

Immediate collection checklist (first 2 hours)
--------------------------------------------
1) Create artifact path and initial manifest (owner: incident commander)
   - s3 path: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/rdx-20260301-001/ (replace with INCIDENT_ID)
   - Create manifest file manifest-<INCIDENT_ID>.yaml with metadata (who, why, timestamp).
2) Capture SLO and error-budget snapshot (owner: SRE oncall)
   - Query SLO service: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://slo.internal.redwood/api/v1/snapshot?service=inference-gateway&window=30d > slo-snapshot.json
   - Rationale: this snapshot is the baseline for post-incident error-budget burn calculations.
3) Export last 48 hours of metrics at 10s resolution for affected services (owner: metrics-worker)
   - prometheus snapshot example:
     curl -sG "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/export" --data-urlencode "query=up{job=\"inference-gateway\"}" --data-urlencode "start=$(date -d '48 hours ago' +%s)" --data-urlencode "end=$(date +%s)" > metrics-inference-gateway-48h.json
4) Capture traces and spans for the incident window (owner: tracing-team)
   - run: otel-collector export with filter service.name in (inference-gateway, model-router) and timeframe = incident_window
   - store as traces-<INCIDENT_ID>.ndjson\n5) Snapshot routing and rollout state (owner: platform-team)
   - kubectl get rollout -n redwood --all-namespaces -o yaml > rollout-state-<INCIDENT_ID>.yaml
   - capture model-router config: curl https://config-store.internal/v1/model-router/config > model-router-config.json\n6) Preserve autoscaler and capacity events (owner: cloud-ops)
   - cloud events: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=ec2.amazonaws.com --start-time "$START" --end-time "$END" > cloud-events.json

Chain-of-custody & Audit Log (must be completed before handoff)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Every action that reads/writes the artifact path must be recorded in the manifest with: actor, timestamp, action, reason, and request-id. Example CSV row appended to manifest-audit.csv:
  timestamp,actor,action,artifact,request_id,notes
  2026-03-01T14:23:45Z,priya.desai,upload,metrics-inference-gateway-48h.json,req-32f4c,initial snapshot
- Access policy: artifacts are encrypted with KMS alias/incident-enc; temporary read grants are given via the incidents IAM role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/incident-worker-<INCIDENT_ID>).
- Do not delete or modify original artifacts. If modification is necessary (e.g., PII redaction), store a copy with clear suffix "-redacted" and log the reason.

Evidence retention and TTLs
--------------------------
- Retention defaults (unless legal hold):
  - Logs and metrics: 90 days
  - Traces/spans: 30 days (but incident exports saved for 365 days)
  - Raw GPU/scheduler profiles: 365 days
  - Model artifacts used in inference: 365 days or as required by model registry policy
- To request extended retention, create ticket in INC-RETENTION with justification and legal approval.

Detailed collection commands (copy-paste ready)
------------------------------------------------
# Create incident path (incident commander)
aws s3api put-object --bucket redwood-incident-artifacts --key rdx-20260301-001/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control
# Export Kubernetes pod logs for inference-gateway (last 24h)
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference-gateway -o name | xargs -I {} kubectl logs {} -n inference --since=24h > /tmp/inference-gateway-logs-24h.log
# Tar and upload
tar -czf /tmp/rdx-20260301-001-evidence.tar.gz /tmp/inference-gateway-logs-24h.log metrics-inference-gateway-48h.json traces-<INCIDENT_ID>.ndjson
aws s3 cp /tmp/rdx-20260301-001-evidence.tar.gz s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/rdx-20260301-001/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/incident-enc\n
If you must redact PII before upload:
- Prefer local redaction and then upload both original encrypted locally and redacted copy with explicit audit entries.
- Redaction example (python):
python - <<'PY'
import re,sys,json
with open('metrics-inference-gateway-48h.json') as f:
    data=f.read()
red=re.sub(r'([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,})','[REDACTED_EMAIL]',data)
with open('metrics-inference-gateway-48h-redacted.json','w') as f:
    f.write(red)
PY

Roles & responsibilities
-------------------------
- Incident Commander: create incident artifact path, ensure manifest exists, verify chain-of-custody.
- SRE Oncall: collect SLO snapshot, metrics, top-level logs, and coordinate with tracing-team.
- Tracing-team: export spans and root-cause traces for the incident window.
- Cloud-ops: collect cloud provider capacity events, autoscaler logs, and VM lifecycle events.
- Platform-team: capture routing and rollout state.
- Legal/Security: approve redaction and extended retention requests.

Post-incident handoff checklist (within 48 hours)
------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm manifest completeness (all artifacts listed and checksum-verified).
   - Example: sha256sum metrics-inference-gateway-48h.json >> manifest-checksums.txt
2) Attach PIR ticket and summary to artifact path (owner: incident commander).
3) Grant read-only access to reviewers (SRE reviewers, service-owner, product, and legal if needed). Use IAM role with duration 8 hours as default.
4) Schedule the post-incident review (PIR) within 7 business days. Attach required artifacts.

Evidence checklist table
------------------------
| Artifact name                         | Required by | Retain (days) | Owner            | Notes |
|---------------------------------------|-------------|---------------|------------------|-------|
| manifest-<INCIDENT_ID>.yaml           | All         | 365           | incident-commander| Metadata + audit CSV |
| slo-snapshot.json                     | SLO        | 365           | SRE oncall       | timestamped snapshot |
| metrics-*-48h.json                    | Capacity   | 90            | metrics-team     | 10s resolution recommended |
| traces-<INCIDENT_ID>.ndjson           | RC root-cause | 365         | tracing-team     | export with sampling preserved |
| rollout-state-<INCIDENT_ID>.yaml      | Platform   | 365           | platform-team    | includes model routing state |
| cloud-events.json                     | Capacity   | 365           | cloud-ops        | autoscale and termination events |
| gpu-profiles-<INCIDENT_ID>.tar.gz     | Perf       | 365           | infra-perf       | scheduler + nvprof outputs |
\nSLO & error-budget notes (how artifacts are used)
---------------------------------------------------
- The SLO snapshot and metrics exports are the canonical inputs to the Error Budget Burn worksheet. The SRE oncall must tag the incident with the SLOs impacted (e.g., inference-gateway: availability 99.95%, latency p99 < 120ms).
- If a retro requires measuring partial-period SLO impact, use slo-snapshot.json and metrics to compute weighted burn. Keep calculation artifacts (notebooks) in the artifact path.

Integration with reliability initiatives and capacity planning
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Use captured capacity events and metrics to populate capacity-runbook templates for recurring incidents. Example: if autoscaler thrash coincides with p95 latency spikes, create a follow-up reliability initiative ticket tagged reliability:autoscale-thrash.
- Attach exported traces to the reliability initiative card to tie causal traces to corrective work (e.g., scale-policy-tuning).

Automation & tooling recommendations
-----------------------------------
- Use incidentctl (internal CLI) to create incident artifact path and template manifest automatically:
  incidentctl create --id rdx-20260301-001 --services inference-gateway,model-router --owner priya.desai
- Incorporate a Lambda function that verifies manifest checksums nightly for active incidents and alerts if any artifact is missing.
- Add a Prometheus alert rule to fire when artifact export jobs fail more than 3 times in 1 hour: rule name: IncidentArtifactExportFailure.

Example manifest (manifest-<INCIDENT_ID>.yaml)
------------------------------------------------
incident_id: rdx-20260301-001
created_by: priya.desai
created_at: 2026-03-01T14:20:00Z
services: [inference-gateway, model-router]
artifacts:
  - name: slo-snapshot.json
    path: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/rdx-20260301-001/slo-snapshot.json
    sha256: <sha256sum>
  - name: metrics-inference-gateway-48h.json
    path: s3://...
    sha256: <sha256sum>
audit_log: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/rdx-20260301-001/manifest-audit.csv

\nAppendix: common troubleshooting snippets
-----------------------------------------
- Check autoscaler pod restarts
  kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=cluster-autoscaler -o wide
- Extract top 100 slowest traces by latency (using internal trace search API):
  curl -sG https://tracing.internal/api/search --data-urlencode "service=inference-gateway" --data-urlencode "sort=-duration" --data-urlencode "limit=100" > top-100-slow-traces.json
